provenance.citation: Kowalski, R., & Sergot, M. (1986). A Logic-based Calculus of Events. New Generation Computing, 4(1), 67–95.
provenance.locus: Sections 2–5: the running office-personnel narrative — 'Mary was hired as a lecturer', 'Mary was promoted to professor' — with events initiating and terminating rank/employment periods; HoldsAt queries over the resulting periods.
provenance.notes: The paper's narrative uses named events E1 (Mary hired as lecturer) and E2 (Mary promoted to professor). Adaptation: integer time points 2 and 5 replace the paper's partially-ordered event tokens (this breed implements the discrete simplified event calculus over a totally ordered timeline). hire initiates employed and lecturer; promote initiates professor and terminates lecturer — exactly the initiates/terminates structure of the paper's example. The asserted period structure matches the paper: lecturer holds between hire and promote (clipped by promotion), professor and employed hold after the promotion.

input.intent: evaluate HoldsAt queries over the Kowalski-Sergot hired/promoted narrative

expected.notes: Lecturer period clipped by the promotion event; professorship and employment persist by inertia.
